sofia (Frontend): Heads up — canary charts got way slower after the runtime merge. LCP/TTFP spikes when switching time ranges, lots of main-thread parse time. :frowning:
jamal (Platform): I saw this too. bundle size +2.3MB on latest canary. webpack-analyzer shows duplicate copy of chart-core in two chunks.
erica (Eng-Platform): Do you have a trace? can you paste the profiler flame? Also which splitpoint changed?
sofia (Frontend): attaching snippet from bundle-analyzer: 
```
chunk A (1.2MB): chart-core (1.1MB)
chunk B (0.9MB): chart-core (1.1MB)
```
sofia (Frontend): suspect dynamic import name collision after we changed lazy-layering (splitpoint revisit) — chunks ended up with the same module in two splits.
jamal (Platform): That would explain double parse. Also telemetry route calls are serializing telemetry during render; if parse doubles, telemetry queues pile up. :eyes: 
mike (SRE): deploy-bot shows canary 2026-06-05-rt-v2.13 deployed at 1768500020
deploy-bot: canary deploy complete (id: canary-rt-v2.13) — health checks passed
erica (Eng-Platform): quick test: on canary, open devtools > network > disable cache, then filter .js and ctrl+f 'chart-core' to see multiple chunk loads. Also check `window.__REDWOOD_CHUNKS__` for duplicate module ids.
sofia (Frontend): did that. both chunks fetched separately and both parsed. call stacks show duplicate registrations.
jamal (Platform): quick workaround: pin lazy-layering flag off in canary rollout (rollout=0.5->0.0) to avoid splitpoint change until we fix naming
erica (Eng-Platform): agree. I'll open a PR to ensure chunk names include component path + hash so no collision. also adding unit test for chunk content dedupe during build.
sofia (Frontend): filed issue: https://github.com/redwood-inference/console/issues/8423 (notes + reproducer)
mike (SRE): rolling canary back now. will monitor latency metrics for 10m. :thumbsup:
sofia (Frontend): thanks. will follow up with a small perf patch and CI bundle check.
